question: Which review schedule maximizes modelled delayed recall of a set of synthetic items under a fixed study budget (a fixed total number of review events within a fixed study window)?
status_label: Simulation study. Independent research manuscript / preprint draft, not peer-reviewed. Simulated learners, not human participants.

experiments.title: Schedule comparison under exponential forgetting (central setting)
experiments.status: confirmatory, complete (250 of 250 runs, 0 excluded, 0 failed)
experiments.verdict: Greedy minus uniform: interval entirely above 0, so the difference is above zero and the directional prediction is supported. The conclusion is restricted to mean recall, because mastery share reverses sign.

estimates.label: greedy minus uniform, minimum item recall

notes: Differences are arm minus uniform over 50 paired simulated learners (seeds 1000 to 1049), with 95% percentile bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples). The effect is small: 0.0162 on a baseline of 0.5327, with standardized paired effect d_z 0.8674.
The greedy scheduler is an oracle: it knows the true model and each item's initial half-life.

experiments.title: Oracle advantage and model misspecification under power-law forgetting
experiments.status: confirmatory, complete (300 of 300 runs, 0 excluded, 0 failed)
experiments.verdict: H0a rejected (greedy with the true power-law model beats uniform). H0b not rejected and its interval lies inside ±0.02 (greedy with a misspecified exponential model is classified as practically equivalent to uniform). Under the frozen interpretation rule, the EXP-001 greedy advantage is declared dependent on model knowledge.
notes: The equivalence classification is fragile (exploratory checks, SENS-001 below): the paired t interval of greedy-exp reaches 0.0201, and on independent seeds the contrast is above 0. The stable finding is the size of the drop, from 0.0347 to 0.0085 (about three quarters).
Both greedy arms still receive each item's true initial half-life.

experiments.title: Optional descriptive check of EXP-002 with ω in {0.3, 3}
experiments.verdict: Not evaluated: the check had no frozen configuration, so it was not run. Sensitivity of every result to the power-law time scale ω is untested.
notes: Recorded as not run in research/freeze.json (post_freeze_record.not_run), the registry, the limitations and the manuscript (section 5.2).

experiments.title: Robustness sweep over models, budgets, retention intervals and item distributions
experiments.status: confirmatory run of a descriptive experiment, complete (18,000 of 18,000 runs, 0 excluded, 0 failed)
experiments.verdict: Descriptive, no hypothesis test. The EXP-001 ranking is not stable: 70 of 72 cells reverse at least one pair of arms, so EXP-001 does not generalize across the sweep.

experiments.title: Exploratory, post hoc sensitivity checks of the three experiments
experiments.status: exploratory, post hoc (specified after the confirmatory results were seen)
experiments.verdict: Changes no frozen verdict. The EXP-001 direction replicates; the EXP-002 equivalence classification is fragile; the EXP-003 instability survives a resolved-difference criterion.

experiments.title: Do the forgetting models predict real first-review recall? (Duolingo traces, held out)
experiments.verdict: No. Neither forgetting model predicts held-out first-review recall better than a constant, so every simulated result is conditional on the assumed memory model.
notes: Held-out trials: 427,005. No interval was computed for these log-loss values.

assumptions.name: Retention interval, RI
assumptions.source: chosen by a pre-stated rule from the uniform arm alone (RI-001); a design choice, not a typical use case

assumptions.name: Power-law time scale, ω
assumptions.source: planning value, not an estimate; sensitivity untested (D-017)

assumptions.name: Scheduler knowledge
assumptions.value: the greedy arms know each item's true initial half-life; EXP-001 greedy also knows the true model

limitations: Simulation only: recall is a model probability, never a human measurement. No claim of human learning gains.
Neither forgetting model beats a constant predictor of held-out real first-review recall (CAL-002); the calibration fixes the time scale of the items, not the shape of forgetting.
The retrieval update ignores the gap since the last review, so the models contain no spacing effect in the psychological sense.
Both greedy arms know each item's true initial half-life; EXP-001's greedy also knows the true model.
Load confound: expanding and massed concentrate all reviews on 4 sessions (peak 50 per session); the other arms use 27 sessions (peak 8).
The central retention interval (281 days) is a design choice; α, β and ω are planning values, and robustness to ω is untested (D-017).
The EXP-002 "equivalent within 0.02" classification sits on the margin and does not replicate on independent seeds or shorter retention intervals (exploratory).
Draft-setting contrasts with the opposite sign were seen before the freeze (disclosed in the freeze record).
EXP-003 has 288 unadjusted arm-versus-uniform intervals; no single cell supports a confirmatory statement. SENS-001 is post hoc.
The calibration data are Duolingo learners and words from 2013; they represent no other population.

calendar.note: Schedule definition at the frozen EXP-001 setting: the fixed arms' plans and the adaptive arms' daily capacity, computed by the committed engine. Which items the adaptive arms review varies by learner. The peak load and sessions used agree with the measured runs.
